rasar.roast_ammo: Rasar paid $73 for Le'Veon Bell in 2018 and got 0.0 fantasy points when Bell held out. He finished last. He also somehow drafted Justin Jefferson for $1 and Ja'Marr Chase for $2 in back-to-back years. The man is capable of brilliance and total catastrophe with equal confidence.

bruce.roast_ammo: Bruce paid $82 for Christian McCaffrey in 2024, a league-record single-player price, and finished last. He also went 1-12 in 2013, still one of the worst records in league history. That $82 is the second-highest single-player price on record, behind only Leems' $84 for CMC in 2020. Bruce commits fully to his studs strategy every year, and the results are historically inconsistent.

worst_seasons.note: Only season below 100 PF/G in 17 years. Made 92 moves. -33.0 DIFF. Worst managed season in league history despite big spend.

signature_moments.note: Worst managed season ever. Paid $77 for Saquon, made 92 moves all year, still tanked.

patterns: High activity manager, lots of adds drops and trades

Usually competitive despite chaotic approach
garrett.roast_ammo: Garrett paid $77 for Saquon Barkley in 2020, made 92 roster moves, and finished with a -33.0 point differential. That is the most active and least effective season in 17 years of this league. Ninety-two moves. Negative 33 points. Do not let him manage your 401k.

signature_moments.outcome: Championship, +24.4 DIFF, only 8 moves all season
signature_moments.note: Won his first championship in approximately a decade of trying. Made 8 total moves. The patience finally paid off.

patterns: Decade of 10th-12th place finishes before 2024
2024 championship with minimal roster moves (8 total)
Quiet low-activity manager who finally found the formula
kevin.roast_ammo: Kevin finished 10th-12th place for most of a decade before winning the 2024 championship with only 8 roster moves and a +24.4 point differential. Either he figured it out or everyone else got worse. The jury is still out on which.

signature_moments.note: Paid $74 for Cee Dee Lamb and $70 for Ja'Marr Chase in the same 2024 draft, $144 on two wide receivers.
Spent $80 on Alvin Kamara in 2019.

patterns: Pays top of the market for elite skill players, usually receivers: Kamara $80 (2019), Chase $75 (2022), Lamb $74 plus Chase $70 (2024)
Routinely spends $64 or more on a single player
cross.roast_ammo: Cross does not wait for value, he pays full retail. He spent $80 on Kamara in 2019, and in 2024 he paid $74 for Cee Dee Lamb and $70 for Ja'Marr Chase in the same draft, $144 on two wide receivers.

signature_moments.note: Paid $40 for LaPorta while Kelce went for $43. LaPorta was not a top-5 TE by any ranking.

patterns: Known to overpay at tight end
2024 LaPorta purchase remains a league talking point
moonshine.roast_ammo: Moonshine paid $40 for Sam LaPorta in 2024, a year where Travis Kelce went for $43. LaPorta is not worth $3 less than Travis Kelce. Moonshine overpaid at TE by approximately $25 and did it with confidence.

reggie.roast_ammo: Reggie had the best season in Nasties history in 2011 with a +35.6 point differential, but is also famous for systematically dismantling Aaron Hendrickson in a trade the league still calls a robbery. Reggie tends to freeze in the first hour of the auction and then wake up mid-draft.

Consistently competitive scorer across all seasons

moe.roast_ammo: Moe has scored more fantasy points than anyone in Nasties history, 27,473.4 all-time. He is remarkably consistent and rarely makes headlines in either direction. In a league full of dramatic characters, Moe is quietly the best scorer the draft never talks about.

robbie.roast_ammo: Robbie has called his team Team Johnson for 17 consecutive years. His team went 2-12 in 2023, the worst record in the 14-game season era. These two facts coexist peacefully.

hendrickson.roast_ammo: Hendrickson is best known in league lore for losing what is widely considered the worst trade in Nasties history to Reggie. He has been in this league for a decade and that trade is still the first thing anyone mentions.

Dropped $78 on David Johnson in 2017.
Paid $75 for Tyreek Hill in 2024, one of at least four drafts where he spent $74 or more on a single player.

patterns: Top-heavy every year: MJD $74 (2010), David Johnson $78 (2017), Antonio Brown $74 (2018), CMC $84 (2020), Tyreek $75 (2024)
Buys two or three studs and lets the back half of the roster go for $1
League member since the beginning (2010)
leems.roast_ammo: Leems has spent $74 or more on a single player in at least four different drafts, topping out at $84 for Christian McCaffrey in 2020, the richest single price in recorded Nasties history. He builds the same team every year: a couple of studs and a bench full of guys making the minimum.

signature_moments.note: Paid $79 for Kamara and $65 for Saquon in the same 2021 draft, then $40 more for Justin Jefferson, leaving $16 for his other eleven roster spots.
Spent $65 on Michael Vick at quarterback in 2011.
Paid $33 for Josh Allen in 2024, two years after paying $39 for him in 2022.

patterns: Panics at QB: $49 Brees (2010), $65 Vick (2011), $41 Rodgers (2013), $39 and $33 Josh Allen (2022, 2024)
Stars-and-scrubs: blows huge money on two or three backs, then fills the roster with $1 fliers
League member since the beginning (2010)
crandall.roast_ammo: Crandall's whole strategy is to spend the GDP of a small country on two running backs and a quarterback, then draft eleven dollar-menu players. In 2021 he paid $79 for Kamara and $65 for Saquon in the same draft. He has paid $33 or more for a quarterback four separate times, including $65 for Michael Vick.

signature_moments.note: Paid $61 for Travis Kelce in 2021, the high point of five straight drafts paying top of the market for the same tight end.
Opened his Nasties career paying $75 for Adrian Peterson in 2010.
Paid $42 for Jimmy Graham in 2012 and $40 again in 2013, the tight-end habit predates Kelce.

patterns: Always pays top of the market for the elite TE: Jimmy Graham ($42, $40), then Travis Kelce ($21, $42, $61, $49, $43 across five drafts)
Buys seven or eight priced starters then throws $1 darts at the bench
League member since the beginning (2010)
shultz.roast_ammo: Shultz has paid up for the number-one tight end every single year for over a decade, Jimmy Graham and then Travis Kelce five drafts running, including a $61 Kelce in 2021. Nobody in the league is more predictable at one position, and everybody still lets him have it.
